title: Local wave-packet spectroscopy of the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
abstract: We investigate wave packets generated by a local pulse electric field in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) with a U(1) charge $q$. Bosonization shows that a local pulse field creates two counterpropagating packets with opposite accumulated charges $\pm qK$ and velocity $v$, where $K$ and $v$ are the TLL parameter and velocity. The packet motion produces a linearly growing charge polarization $P(t)=2 qDt$ in the conducting TLL at non-equilibrium, allowing the Drude weight $D=vK$ to be extracted from real-time local dynamics. We test this local-packet description by time-dependent variational principle simulations of the spin-1/2 XXZ chain. The simulations visualize the density, current, energy, and entanglement profiles in the space-time plane and confirm the predicted packet charge and propagation velocity. We also show that excess energy and entanglement remaining near the pulse region are suppressed in the weak-pulse limit. Finally, the Drude weight obtained from the packet-induced polarization agrees with the exact Bethe-ansatz result, demonstrating local-packet spectroscopy of intrinsic transport in a TLL.
summary: This paper develops a method to measure the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids by observing the ballistic separation of charge wave packets induced by a local electric pulse. Using TDVP simulations on the XXZ chain, the authors show that the linear growth of the induced charge polarization directly yields the Drude weight, confirming the theoretical predictions even in non-integrable models.
main_problem: The study investigates how a local perturbation generates and propagates wave packets in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) and relates this dynamics to the intrinsic transport coefficient, the Drude weight.
main_result: The linear-in-time growth of the charge polarization, $P(t) \propto t$, allows for the extraction of the Drude weight, $D=vK$, which is shown to agree with exact theoretical results.
method: The analysis combines bosonization theory with numerical simulations using the Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) applied to the spin-1/2 XXZ chain.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the spin-1/2 XXZ chain, which serves as a prototypical TLL. The Hamiltonian is analyzed in the gapless regime, and the study extends to the non-integrable $J_1-J_2$ XXZ model.
key_observables: Charge polarization $P(t)$, excess energy density ($\Delta E_\ell$), excess entanglement entropy ($\Delta S_\ell$), and the Drude weight ($D$).
important_parameters: TLL parameter ($K$), velocity ($v$), and the width ($\ell$) of the local pulse perturbation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the low-energy physics is accurately described by the TLL fixed point, and that the linear growth of polarization directly yields the Drude weight.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the local pulse protocol, the space-time profiles of density and current, the linear growth of polarization $P(t)$, and the decay of excess energy and entanglement entropy with the pulse width $\ell$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using bosonization to predict packet dynamics. It then applies this to the integrable XXZ chain using TDVP simulations to confirm the Drude weight extraction. Finally, it extends the analysis to the non-integrable $J_1-J_2$ model, confirming the robustness of the wave-packet picture.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel, real-space, time-domain probe (local-packet spectroscopy) to measure a bulk transport property (Drude weight) in strongly correlated quantum materials, complementing standard uniform-current response measurements.

(b) Illustration of the electric field E(x, t), applied to the interval I with width ℓin the one-dimensional chain.

FIG. 2. Time evolution of (a)(e) spin density, (b)(f) current density, (c)(g) excess energy density, and (d)(h) excess bipartition entanglement entropy in the space-time plane. The twist width and system size are fixed at ℓ= 18 and L = 200, respectively. (a)–(d) ∆= 0.4 (antiferromagnetic). (e)–(h) ∆= −0.4 (ferromagnetic).

FIG. 3. (a) Packet charge Qright (red circles) and Qleft (blue squares) as a function of the Luttinger parameter K, evaluated from the relaxed states. The dotted lines are linear fits, Qright = 1.00K and Qleft = −1.02K. (b) Packet width W and (c) packet height h of the right (red circles) and left (blue squares) packets. W is the full width at half maximum of the Sz j after Gaussian smoothing (σ = 2 sites), and h is the average of the unsmoothed Sz j within this width. Both are averaged over 25 ≤t ≤30. The dashed lines in (c) are linear fits. The gray dotted lines show W = ℓin (b) and h = ±K/ℓin (c). The twist width is ℓ= 18 and the system size is L = 100.

FIG. 4. (a) Twist width ℓdependence of the excess energy density. The fitting line is ∆Eℓ∝1/ℓ1.99. (b) Twist width ℓ dependence of the excess entanglement entropy. The fitting is performed using ∆Sℓ∼a log ℓ/ℓ2 + b/ℓ2. The interaction is ∆= 0.4, and the system size is L = 100. These data are averaged over 30 ≤t ≤40, by which the wave packets have sufficiently relaxed and their profiles have reached a steady form.
